title: Milestone: Animals With Backbones
objective: After this level you can connect mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians and fish into one family tree.
summary: Five vertebrate groups share one backbone; mammals and birds make their own heat, the rest mostly take it from outside. Fish are the biggest branch: about 37,000 of about 76,000 described species.

cards.headline: Milestone: halfway to Mastery. Five groups, one backbone.
cards.body: Back in Level 3 you ran a finger down your spine: your membership card. Mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians and fish all carry one, a column of vertebrae around the spinal cord. This chapter spent its time with the biggest branch of that family. Time to see the whole backbone family at once.

cards.headline: One backbone family, sorted by heat

items.label: No backbone at all
points: This chapter's jellyfish and sea stars

cards.fact: Nearly half of all vertebrate species are fish.
cards.context: IUCN's 2025 table counts about 76,000 described vertebrate species, and about 37,000 of them are fish. Put every mammal, bird, reptile and amphibian species together and they only just outnumber the fish. From Level 41's gills to Level 47's salmon, this chapter covered the backbone family's biggest branch.

mascot.line: Everyone photographs the lions, and meanwhile the fish quietly win the headcount.

cards.headline: Milestone: backbones connected
learned: How fish breathe the oxygen dissolved in water, and what makes a shark different from a bony fish.
Why tiny drifting plankton hold up the whole ocean food web and make much of Earth's oxygen.
How deep-sea animals live far from sunlight, and why so many of them make their own light.
Why corals and jellyfish count as animals, and what makes a stressed coral turn white.

questions.prompt: Animals With Backbones milestone: what does a vertebrate's backbone partly enclose?

options.label: The heart and lungs
options.rationale: The backbone encloses the spinal cord, not those.

options.label: The stomach
options.rationale: The backbone encloses the spinal cord.

options.label: The gills
options.rationale: Gills are for breathing; the backbone holds the spinal cord.

questions.explanation: Vertebrae form a column that partly encloses the central nervous system, including the spinal cord.

questions.prompt: Animals With Backbones milestone, from Level 41: how does a fish take in oxygen?
questions.explanation: Water flows over the gill filaments, and dissolved oxygen passes into the blood.

questions.prompt: Animals With Backbones milestone, from Level 42: what makes a shark's skeleton unusual for a vertebrate?

options.label: It is made of shell, like a crab's
options.rationale: Sharks have cartilage, not a shell.

options.label: It is outside the body
options.rationale: Sharks have an inside skeleton of cartilage.

options.label: It has no backbone
options.rationale: Sharks are fish, and fish are vertebrates.

questions.explanation: Sharks have no bones: their skeleton is cartilage.

questions.prompt: Animals With Backbones milestone: about what share of described vertebrate species are fish?

options.label: About 90 percent
options.rationale: Too high; the other four groups add up to a bit more.

questions.explanation: About 37,000 of about 76,000 described vertebrate species are fish: nearly half.

questions.prompt: Animals With Backbones milestone: which pair of vertebrate groups makes its own body heat?
questions.explanation: Mammals and birds are endotherms; fish, amphibians and reptiles mostly take heat from their surroundings.

questions.prompt: Animals With Backbones milestone, from Level 47: what guides an adult salmon back to its home stream?

options.label: Following older salmon
options.rationale: It navigates by its own memory.

options.label: The stars at night
options.rationale: It follows smell, plus a magnetic clue.

options.label: The warmest water it can find
options.rationale: It follows the smell of home.

options.label: Its memory of the stream's smell

questions.explanation: Young salmon imprint on their stream's odor and use that memory to home as adults.

questions.prompt: Animals With Backbones milestone: which of these ocean animals is a vertebrate?
questions.explanation: A shark is a fish, and fish are one of the five vertebrate groups, even with a skeleton of cartilage.
